active_paradigms.idea: Use exact permutation enumeration on conflict components that are small enough, extending the current n<=8 exact regime to every isolated hard core
active_paradigms.description: The current program first removes disconnected read/write-conflict components, then uses a randomized prefix beam and relocation descent for every component larger than eight transactions. Its strength is that every acceptance decision uses workload.get_opt_seq_cost, but its weakness is irreversible beam pruning: the cost of a partial prefix is not a reliable predictor of its final conflict critical path, so good orientations can disappear early. For each connected component with at most roughly 10-11 transactions, call itertools.permutations on its local transaction ids and evaluate every complete permutation through the simulator cache; choose the true minimum rather than applying beam search. Keep the existing component mapping, but select the factorial cutoff from an explicit evaluation budget, e.g. do exact search when factorial(component_size) is below a fixed number of simulator calls. This is especially valuable because sparse workloads commonly split into cores whose size is just above the current cutoff, where 9! or 10! direct evaluations are practical and remove heuristic error entirely. For components above the cutoff, retain the existing heuristic fallback rather than spending the whole timeout on one core. This differs from the failed MILP attempt because it does not approximate the simulator's nonlinear objective or attempt an invalid longest-path linearization: it directly optimizes the exact evaluator objective.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary makespan only, by replacing approximate schedules with provably optimal schedules on all tractable conflict components.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not enumerate globally unless the global factorial count is within budget. Cache complete permutations and avoid using partial-sequence cost as a proof-quality pruning bound unless monotonicity with respect to the simulator has been verified. The assembled order must still consist of original parent transaction ids.

active_paradigms.idea: Use a discrete tabu search with direct simulator scoring and conflict-aware large neighborhoods, rather than the current short relocation descent
active_paradigms.description: The existing local search examines one-transaction relocations, permits only a few neutral moves, and stops after at most min(3*n,30) iterations. That makes it fast and deterministic, but it cannot cross a basin requiring several worsening moves, and a relocation often leaves most pairwise conflict directions unchanged. Replace the refinement phase by a tabu search implemented with a fixed-size tabu queue keyed by recently reversed transaction pairs; at each iteration evaluate a sampled neighborhood containing adjacent swaps, arbitrary swaps, and 2- or 3-transaction block moves. Select the lowest-cost admissible neighbor even when it is worse than the current schedule, unless a tabu move beats the global incumbent (aspiration criterion). Bias the sampled moves toward pairs that share at least one key with a write, because swapping nonconflicting transactions cannot change the serial conflict orientation and need not consume simulator evaluations. Periodically diversify by selecting a short contiguous conflict-dense block, permuting that block, and continue tabu search from the best such candidate; all ranking remains based on get_opt_seq_cost. Maintain an incumbent separately from the current state, use a deterministic seed, and allocate a fixed simulator-evaluation budget so the routine remains predictable. This is fundamentally discrete direct search, unlike the failed continuous random-key dual annealing, and it addresses precisely the current program's inability to traverse worsening paths.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary makespan, particularly schedules trapped in local minima under single relocations and limited equal-cost plateau walks.
active_paradigms.cautions: A tabu search must score full schedules with the simulator; do not substitute transaction length or graph degree as its acceptance objective. Never forbid an improving move via tabu status, bound cache memory, and use an evaluation-count termination condition rather than an unbounded loop. For very large n, sample only conflict-bearing moves rather than O(n^2) swaps per iteration.

active_paradigms.idea: Use sparse spectral ordering of a simulator-calibrated signed conflict matrix to create structurally different high-quality starting schedules
active_paradigms.description: The current construction phase ranks candidate next transactions by the simulator cost of a prefix, which is myopic because later transactions can create long critical paths through several earlier conflict orientations. Build a sparse pairwise conflict matrix from the workload text: for each transaction pair that has a read/write or write/write overlap, estimate which relative order is preferable by comparing the simulator cost of a small number of complete probe schedules that differ only by that pair's order. Accumulate the signed preference and confidence into a symmetric sparse Laplacian, then call scipy.sparse.linalg.eigsh for its Fiedler vector; sorting transactions by that vector yields a global seriation that places mutually compatible precedence preferences consistently along one axis. Evaluate both vector directions and, when confidence is weak, several deterministic tie-break variants, all using the actual simulator, and use the best as a candidate schedule. This directly targets cyclic and long-range conflict structure that prefix beam search misses, while allowing the existing simulator-based refinement to decide whether the structural prediction was useful. It is different from the failed SCC decomposition because it does not merely identify components; it computes a global ordering signal inside a connected conflict core. It is also not an MILP or continuous permutation optimizer: the eigenvector is only a graph-structural ordering construction based on measured pairwise simulator effects.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary makespan through better initial orientations of many conflict edges simultaneously, increasing the chance that subsequent direct local search reaches a better basin.
active_paradigms.cautions: The signed matrix must use only true read/write or write/write conflict pairs; read/read overlaps must contribute nothing. Pair probes should be few and deterministic because O(n^2) full evaluations may be expensive. eigsh requires handling tiny components and disconnected/zero matrices explicitly, and the final choice must always be made by get_opt_seq_cost rather than by the spectral surrogate.

tried_paradigms.idea: Formulate the transaction-ordering problem as a direct mixed-integer longest-path scheduling model with scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is a simulator-driven randomized beam search followed by relocation descent and small ruin-and-recreate moves. Its important strength is that every ordering decision is evaluated by workload.get_opt_seq_cost, so it optimizes the true scalar rather than transaction size or write counts; its principal weakness is that prefix beam pruning and one-transaction relocations cannot jointly reverse a large set of interacting conflict directions. Build a MILP whose binary variables x[i,j] choose whether transaction i precedes transaction j for each relevant conflicting pair, with antisymmetry and transitivity/order-rank constraints. Reconstruct the operation precedence DAG implied by each transaction's internal operation chain and the selected read/write or write/write conflict directions, then introduce start-time variables and a makespan variable constrained by every precedence edge. Minimize that makespan directly using scipy.optimize.milp, and return transactions sorted by the solved integer ranks. Use the simulator only to verify the returned ordering and, if its exact semantics reveal a mismatch, add the missing precedence constraints rather than tuning heuristics. This is fundamentally stronger than beam search because it optimizes coupled conflict orientations globally instead of committing to them from partial prefixes.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The sole primary objective: the simulator makespan returned by workload.get_opt_seq_cost, and therefore the aggregate scalar score over the evaluator workloads.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This requires inspecting txn_simulator semantics before encoding constraints: reads may conflict differently depending on whether the simulator uses locks, version dependencies, or transaction-level serialization. Do not include transitivity constraints for every triple on large instances unless necessary; use integer rank variables plus indicator/big-M constraints, or restrict pair variables to transaction pairs that actually share a key with at least one write. Big-M must safely exceed the longest possible operation schedule. Always preserve original transaction-internal operation order and convert ranks into a complete permutation with deterministic tie handling.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use networkx.algorithms.components.strongly_connected_components to identify conflict-coupled scheduling cores and spend exact search budget only where order can matter
tried_paradigms.description: The present search treats all transactions as equally coupled, samples only 24 candidates on large prefixes, and evaluates many relocations that may reverse no real read/write dependency. First construct a directed interaction representation from the workload: connect two transactions when they access a common key and at least one access is a write, while retaining per-key access information to distinguish actual conflict density. Apply networkx.algorithms.components.strongly_connected_components after orienting a provisional conflict graph from a simulator-scored seed order, so groups whose orientations mutually constrain one another become explicit hard cores. For each hard core small enough for exhaustive permutation search, enumerate its internal orders under fixed external boundary ranks and retain its simulator-best orientation; transactions outside such cores should be placed by their actual marginal simulator cost, not arbitrary beam-prefix survival. The key structural observation is that nonconflicting transactions cannot improve makespan through their relative order, whereas dense cores dominate the critical path and need joint moves much larger than the current three-transaction ruin. This can expose conflict clusters that the current random relocation search almost never flips simultaneously. Compare complete assembled schedules with workload.get_opt_seq_cost and retain only the actual best one.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Critical-path reductions caused by jointly changing the orientation of dense read/write conflict clusters, while avoiding simulator evaluations on independent or weakly coupled transaction pairs.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A shared read-read key is not an edge and must not merge components. Strong components are a search-budget decomposition aid, not a proof that separately optimized component schedules compose optimally if the simulator has any global resource contention; final schedules must therefore always be rescored by get_opt_seq_cost. If an initial orientation makes the directed graph artificially acyclic, also consider undirected connected components as a conservative grouping fallback. Do not assume transaction IDs or textual operation lengths carry useful priority information.

tried_paradigms.idea: Apply scipy.optimize.dual_annealing directly to a continuous random-key encoding of complete transaction permutations, scored exclusively by the simulator
tried_paradigms.description: The current method is deterministic after one fixed seed and is dominated by local insertion neighborhoods; even its plateau moves change only one transaction at a time. Represent a candidate permutation by n continuous random keys, decode it as the transaction indices sorted by key, and define the objective as workload.get_opt_seq_cost of that decoded permutation. Call scipy.optimize.dual_annealing once with bounds [0,1] for every key and a fixed reproducible seed; this directly searches full permutations through occasional large coordinated rank changes rather than through beam-prefix commitments. Cache decoded permutations because many different key vectors induce the same ordering, and return the best decoded schedule observed by the objective. The simulator remains the objective oracle, so this method does not rely on an inaccurate proxy such as number of writes, graph degree, or operation count. Compared with the existing local search, annealing can cross high-cost intermediate schedules and reach an ordering basin requiring several conflict directions to change together. A modest polishing pass is unnecessary for the concept and should not replace the annealer's returned best schedule; the solver's best simulator-scored permutation is the output.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape from the local minima and equal-cost plateaus produced by relocation descent, seeking lower true simulator makespan through global coordinated permutation changes.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Sorting random keys makes the objective piecewise constant with discontinuities, so configure a sufficiently high evaluation budget and use caching; it is a stochastic global discrete search, not a smooth continuous optimization claim. Bound cache memory as the current program does. Keep the seed fixed if evaluator consistency matters, and impose a time-aware maximum number of simulator evaluations because full schedule scoring may dominate runtime. For very small n, exhaustive enumeration remains preferable because it proves optimality.

tried_paradigms.idea: Formulate the transaction-order and operation-timing problem as an exact mixed-integer linear program with scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: The current program uses simulator-scored beam construction followed by sampled relocation descent and small ruin-and-recreate moves. Its main strength is that every accepted comparison uses workload.get_opt_seq_cost, but it spends many evaluations on partial-prefix scores and random neighborhoods that need not expose the globally important conflict orientations. Build a disjunctive precedence model whose continuous variables are start/completion times for every operation and whose binary variables x[i,j] choose whether transaction i precedes transaction j. Add transaction-internal precedence edges, and for every cross-transaction read/write or write/write conflict add the appropriate big-M precedence constraint activated by x[i,j] or x[j,i]. Add antisymmetry and transitivity/linear-order constraints for the x variables, then minimize a makespan variable constrained above every operation completion time. For modest workloads, scipy.optimize.milp can therefore optimize all conflict directions jointly rather than committing to them greedily; extract transaction ranks from the binary solution and validate that order once with get_opt_seq_cost. This is especially valuable when a bad decision near the beam prefix has a delayed effect that relocation search cannot repair without several worsening moves.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The exact primary simulator makespan, by jointly selecting conflict orientations and operation critical-path timing rather than optimizing a proxy such as transaction length or prefix cost.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This is exact only if the simulator is an earliest-start schedule over unit-duration operation precedence constraints; first inspect its conflict semantics, operation durations, and tie handling and reproduce them exactly. Use a safe finite M based on the total number/duration of all operations, not an arbitrary huge number, and impose x[i,j]+x[j,i]=1 only for distinct transactions. MILP size is quadratic in transactions and can be large for dense workloads, so use it for bounded-size connected conflict components or enforce a solver time limit and retain the best incumbent.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use critical-path conflict-block neighborhoods identified with networkx.algorithms.dag.longest_path
tried_paradigms.description: The present descent samples arbitrary relocations, so the overwhelming majority of evaluated moves often alter conflicts that have slack and cannot improve makespan. For each incumbent order, reconstruct the directed operation graph used by the simulator: transaction sequence edges plus cross-transaction conflict edges implied by the order. Call networkx.algorithms.dag.longest_path with operation duration weights to obtain the current critical path, and mark every transaction and cross-transaction conflict edge appearing on that path. Generate a large neighborhood that reorders only a contiguous critical block, reverses the order of one critical conflicting pair, or ejects a critical transaction and tests all insertions around the transactions connected to it. Evaluate every resulting complete order with get_opt_seq_cost and keep the best strict improvement; rebuild the critical path after every accepted change. This directly attacks the arcs that determine the returned makespan, unlike the current equal-cost random plateau walks, while preserving the simulator as the authoritative objective. It also gives a principled way to choose ruin-and-recreate removals: remove transactions participating in the greatest number of critical-path conflicts rather than uniformly random transactions.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Makespan reductions caused by shortening the actual critical precedence chain; evaluation effort is concentrated on zero-slack read/write and write/write dependencies.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The graph construction must match simulator semantics exactly, including whether a conflict is between particular operations or all accesses to an item and how same-time ties are resolved. A longest path can contain only one of several tied critical paths, so collect critical nodes/edges from repeated forward/backward slack calculations or rotate among tied paths rather than repeatedly optimizing one arbitrary path. Do not accept a graph-estimated improvement without simulator validation, because the simulator may contain scheduling details not represented in the reconstructed graph.

tried_paradigms.idea: Decompose independent conflict components with scipy.sparse.csgraph.connected_components before spending search budget
tried_paradigms.description: Construct an undirected transaction conflict graph with an edge exactly when two transactions access a common key and at least one of those accesses is a write. The current beam treats all n! orders as one coupled problem even when many transactions have no possible precedence interaction, which wastes width and relocation evaluations deciding irrelevant relative positions. Convert this graph to a sparse adjacency matrix and call scipy.sparse.csgraph.connected_components to identify independent transaction groups. Transactions in different components have no read/write or write/write edge, so their mutual ordering cannot change any conflict orientation; optimize each component independently using exhaustive enumeration, MILP, or the existing simulator-scored search according to component size. Concatenate component schedules in any deterministic order, or interleave them only for bookkeeping, and verify the assembled schedule with the simulator. This transforms the exponential search dimension from n into the size of the largest true conflict component and permits exact solution of many components that the current code would only heuristically search. Even when there is one large component, articulation-like weakly linked regions revealed by this graph are useful for allocating beam width and restart effort to the dense core instead of isolated transactions.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Search scalability and consistency of the primary makespan by eliminating order decisions that provably cannot affect read/write conflict dependencies.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not create graph edges for read/read sharing, since those operations do not conflict. This decomposition is valid only if get_opt_seq_cost has no hidden global resource, transaction-start serialization, or ordering penalty beyond the stated item conflicts; test that swapping transactions from two different components leaves cost unchanged before relying on it. If the simulator uses the supplied sequence to impose a dependency even for nonconflicting transactions, components must not be solved and concatenated as independent schedules.
